conflicts.description: The Helm Council demands that the elevators be restored under the charter, while the Verdant Assembly holds food and water hostage until its terms are met. Each side has people who would escalate.
conflicts.name: The Elevator Standoff

conflicts.description: The Cinder Union must choose between loyalty to the Helm Council and a deal with Ring Seven that would improve its shares, and its decision could tip the standoff.
conflicts.name: The Foundry Choice

conflicts.description: Both governments pressure the Tether Wardens to close or open the cable crossings, and the guild is split between neutrality and picking a side.
conflicts.name: The Wardens' Burden

description: The generation ship Meridian Ark is a vast rotating vessel built from stacked habitable tiers, each a rotating ring linked by long spine elevators that carry people, water, and power. Four generations into a voyage that will last six more, the seventh ring has declared independence and severed the elevators that connect the habitable tiers. The result is a tense, claustrophobic science fiction setting where every decision carries the risk of a hull breach, a famine, or a blockade. The seventh ring holds the ship's primary hydroponic and reclamation systems, so its secession turns food, air, and ballast water into political weapons. Life aboard is shaped by rationed spin gravity, brittle diplomacy, and the awareness that there is nowhere to flee. Original details include tether-wardens who keep emergency cable crossings alive, a ledger-based currency measured in liters of reclaimed air, and a culture in which every citizen is bound to a ring of birth. The ring that secedes is not just a place but a statement that the voyage's founding charter no longer binds anyone.

factions.description: The hereditary governing body of the Meridian Ark, sworn to the founding charter and committed to restoring the elevators by negotiation or, failing that, force.
factions.name: Helm Council

factions.description: The elected body of Ring Seven that declared independence. It demands a renegotiated charter, fair resource shares, and recognition as a sovereign ring.
factions.name: Verdant Assembly

factions.description: A neutral guild of cable riders and hull technicians who maintain emergency crossings and refuse to side with either government, though both try to recruit them.
factions.name: Tether Wardens

factions.description: A labor coalition of foundry and reactor workers who are weighing a strike or an alliance with Ring Seven to secure better allotments.
factions.name: Cinder Union

history.description: The Meridian Ark left its home system under the founding charter, which divided labor and resources among the rings.
history.name: The Departure

history.description: A crop blight in Ring Seven caused years of rationing in the other rings and left lasting resentment over how shortages were handled.
history.name: The Lean Winter

history.description: A failed elevator coupling killed dozens and showed how fragile the connections between rings were, which led to the creation of the Tether Wardens.
history.name: The Spine Collapse of Hollow Sixteen

history.description: Ring Seven's Assembly announced independence and cut the elevators in a single coordinated hour.
history.name: The Verdancy Declaration

locations.description: The first ring, home to the navigation core, the ship's archives, and the Charter Chamber. Its corridors are quiet, formal, and heavily monitored. From here the Helm Council tries to keep the voyage on course while coping with the loss of the seventh ring.
locations.name: Helm Ring

locations.description: A crowded industrial ring of foundries, fabrication halls, and reactor tenders. Its workers are exhausted and increasingly sympathetic to the seventh ring's complaints about unequal rationing.
locations.name: Cinder Ring

locations.description: The seventh ring, a green, humid belt of terraced farms, reclamation vats, and ballast reservoirs. Its citizens control the ship's food and water cycles and have severed all elevator links to enforce their independence.
locations.name: Verdancy, Ring Seven

locations.description: The cut elevator shafts and dangling cable crossings between the tiers. Tether-wardens keep a few improvised ring-to-ring transit lines alive here, and the zone is the most dangerous place on the ship, as it is exposed to vacuum, cold, and shifting gravity.
locations.name: The Severed Spine

name: The Tessellate Ring

rules.statement: Each ring's gravity depends on its spin rate. Slowing a ring to conserve energy weakens its gravity, and abrupt changes can injure residents and strain the structure.
Air, water, and nutrients circulate in a closed loop across the whole ship, so any ring that stops sharing starves the others within weeks.
Only the spine elevators can move bulk cargo and large numbers of people between rings. Cable crossings carry a handful of travelers at a time.
Rations and labor credits are tracked in liters of reclaimed air, and a citizen with a negative balance loses access to ring services.
Citizens are bound by charter to the ring of their birth and need Helm Council approval to transfer, a rule the Verdant Assembly now rejects.
Open flame and explosive propellants are banned throughout the vessel, and weapons are limited to stun lances, pressure tools, and hull-safe projectors.
